newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Commission to be reimbursed for asbestos claim.
newsitem.headline: Court says Commission to be reimbursed for asbestos claim.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ordered insurance companies on Thursday to reimburse the European Commission more than 26 million Belgian francs paid to a former employee who contracted lung disease after exposure to asbestos.

The court found Royale Belge, Assurances Generales de France and six other insurers contractually liable for monies paid by the Commission to Mr. X, after a medical committee ruled he contracted lung cancer and chronic asthmatoid bronchitis from exposure to asbestos at the Berlaymont building in Brussels.

Mr. X asked that these diseases be considered occupational diseases for insurance purposes, and after a first denial by a Commission appointed doctor, a medical committee concluded his cancer was an occupational disease.

The Commission in May 1994 awarded Mr. X the amount of 25,794,194 francs, a 130 percent allowance. The court is ordering insurers to pay back this amount, plus interest at the rate of eight percent since May, 1994.
Royal Belge unsuccessfully argued the Commission failed to give it proper notice before paying out the award.

"It appears the insurers had the opportunity to put further questions to the medical committee ... yet they confined themselves to stating an intention to put such question without actng on it, thus missing an opportunity," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Officials - Insurance against accidents and occupational diseases"
Commission of the European Communities, applicant

application for an order that the insurers pay the Commission the lump sum allegedly due from the Commission to one of its officials on the ground of occupational illness by virtue of article 73 of the Staff Regulations of officials of the European Communities

1. Orders Royale Belge SA, Assurances Generale de France SA, Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance, Les Mutuelles du Mans, Assurantie van de Belgische Boerenbond SA, Hannover SA, Securitas AG and Condor to pay the Commission the sum of BF 25,794,194 plus interest at the rate of 8 percent from 6 May 1994;

2. Orders Royale Belge SA, Assurances Generale de France SA, Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance, Les Mutuelles du Mans, Assurantie van de Belgische Boerenbond SA, Hannover SA, Securitas AG and Condor to pay the costs.
